bibl.title: Behavioral Strategy Determines Frontal or Posterior Location of Short-Term Memory in Neocortex

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: in mammalian neocortex remains elusive. Here we show that distinct neocortical areas maintain short-term memory depending on behavioral strategy. Using wide-field and single-cell calcium imaging,

span.label: short-term memory localisation in mouse neocortex
span.quote: The location of short-term memory in mammalian neocortex remains elusive.

span.label: calcium-imaging
span.quote: Using wide-field and single-cell calcium imaging, we measured layer 2/3 neuronal activity in mice performing a whisker-based texture discrimination task with delayed response.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Posterior parietal area RL, which projects both frontally to M2 and posteriorly to area P, routes the sensory information to one destination or the other according to the animal's behavioural state
span.quote: Therefore, they could route information to either frontal or posterior cortices depending on the mouse’s state.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: When information is held frontally in M2, posterior cortex is actively suppressed below baseline, which is why the two memory patterns are mutually exclusive
span.quote: The latter observation suggests that posterior areas may be inhibited when information is maintained in M2 (Allen et al., 2017).

span.label: Wide-field signals are bulk population signals that may be confounded by non-neuronal fluorescence
span.note: what this limits: every signal reported: WIDE-FIELD FLUORESCENCE SIGNALS REPRESENT BULK SIGNALS, SUMMED OVER NEURONAL POPULATIONS (AS WELL AS POTENTIALLY CONFOUNDED BY NON-NEURONAL FLUORESCENCE CHANGES, WHICH NEEDS TO BE CONTROLLED FOR)
span.quote: The disadvantage of the method is that the wide-field fluorescence signals represent bulk signals, summed over neuronal populations (as well as potentially confounded by non-neuronal fluorescence changes, which needs to be controlled for).

span.label: Only layer 2/3 was studied; other layers may behave differently
span.note: what this limits: the laminar reach of the conclusions: THIS STUDY FOCUSED ON LAYER 2/3 NEURONS, WHEREAS OTHER LAYERS MAY CONTRIBUTE DIFFERENTLY TO TASK-RELATED PROCESSES
span.quote: In addition, this study focused on layer 2/3 neurons, whereas other layers may contribute differently to task-related processes (Chandrasekaran et al., 2017; van Kerkoerle et al., 2014; Li et al., 2015).

span.label: The identity of the posterior activation spot is uncertain and may include neighbouring areas
span.note: what this limits: the anatomical identity of the posterior activation: GIVEN THE VARIABILITY AMONG ANIMALS ... THE OBSERVED ACTIVATION SPOT MAY ALSO ENCOMPASS ADJACENT POSTERIOR AREAS SUCH AS LATEROMEDIAL VISUAL CORTEX OR POSTRHINAL CORTICES
span.quote: Given the variability among animals, however, the observed activation spot may also encompass adjacent posterior areas such as lateromedial visual cortex or postrhinal cortices.

span.label: The proposed what/where pathway interpretation is not directly tested here
span.note: what this limits: the what/where pathway interpretation: ADDITIONAL EXPERIMENTS DIRECTLY TESTING EACH PATHWAY WILL BE NEEDED TO SUBSTANTIATE THESE IDEAS
span.quote: Nevertheless, additional experiments directly testing each pathway will be needed to substantiate these ideas.

span.label: The measurement is a bulk signal, and the authors state they cannot exclude having missed intermingled subpopulations averaged out within it.
span.note: what this limits: the absence of task-relevant activity in an area of these maps: the signal is a bulk population measure and the authors state intermingled subpopulations could be averaged out within it
span.quote: wide-field fluorescence signals represent bulk signals, summed over neuronal populations (as well as potentially confounded by non-neuronal fluorescence changes, which needs to be controlled for). We therefore cannot exclude the possibility that we have missed intermingled sub- 28 populations of neurons that carry task-relevant information but are averaged out in the population signal.

span.label: The grouping variable the entire result rests on is, in some sessions, assigned by a substitute measure whose accuracy is stated as 75%.
span.note: what this limits: the active/passive trial labels in this study: in sessions without usable body-camera images they were predicted from a z-axis focus drop, reported at 75% accuracy against the camera
span.quote: For a small subset of sessions where the body camera gave low quality images or was missing, we predicted the mouse’s movement based on the z-axis drop in focus (using a 10% drop from baseline in 3 in-focus single cells as criterion; 75% accuracy in labeling trials by validating with move vector from the body camera

span.label: The independent variable is changed by the manipulation. Strategy is treated as what determines where short-term memory sits, but optogenetic silencing of the site induces strategy switches that persist across days and appear in non-perturbation trials. The paper reports this as a result rather than as a threat, and it is the correct reading - but it means strategy and site are mutually determining, not one prior to the other, and the title states only one direction.
span.quote: Here, we find that some mice manage to maintain relatively high performance despite perturbation of one area (M2 or P) whereas other mice show significantly reduced performance. The former mice apparently flexibly switch to the alternative unperturbed strategy whereas the latter mice maintain their strategy. Strategy switches were consistent across days, present also in trials without perturbation and were clearly reflected in corresponding switches between M2- and P-dominated delay maps.

span.label: Two thresholds on the same movement signal do different jobs: one splits trials into active and passive by movement during the sensation period, the other discards trials with movement in the first second of the delay as noisy. The grouping rule and the exclusion rule read the same measure, so which trials survive is not independent of which class they were assigned to.
span.quote: Dashed black line indicates threshold to construct the corresponding binary movement vectors (lower black traces). Classification into active (dark green) and passive (light green) trials is based on movement during the sensation period. Trials with the mouse moving during the first second in the delay period were defined as noisy and discarded (bottom trial).

span.label: a set of control experiments on the imaging signal itself
span.note: eliminates: autofluorescence and non-calcium-related intrinsic signals as the source of the measured activity
span.quote: In control experiments we excluded confounding effects of autofluorescence or non-calcium-related intrinsic signals (STAR Methods and Figure S3).

span.label: control imaging targeted at the near-midline M2 area, which lies close to the superior sagittal sinus
span.note: eliminates: hemodynamic signal as the source of the activity patterns, in the one location where a blood vessel makes it most likely
span.quote: In control experiments, we verified that these activity patterns were not confounded by hemodynamic signals, especially for the near-midline M2 area, which is close to the superior sagittal sinus (Figures S3 and S8).

span.label: training two wild-type mice - carrying no GCaMP - on the same task and imaging them awake and performing
span.note: eliminates: autofluorescence, by running the whole experiment in animals that cannot produce the signal of interest
span.quote: 2) To control for autofluorescence signals we trained 2 wild-type mice on the task and obtained wide-field imaging in awake performing animals (Figure S3A-D).

span.label: cellular-resolution imaging run alongside the wide-field measurement
span.note: eliminates: the possibility that the bulk population signal is not driven by the layer 2/3 cell bodies it is interpreted as reflecting
span.quote: In summary, the results from all the above control experiments indicate no major influence of non-calcium-related intrinsic signals on the GCaMP6f signals that would confound our signal interpretations.

span.label: four experiments on the light delivery, including shining light on cortex not expressing ArchT in the same mice - one record for the set, quoting the sentence that reports the outcome
span.note: eliminates: light disturbance itself as the cause of the behavioural effect, and establishes that the effect requires the right population at the right time
span.quote: In summary, these control experiments demonstrate that light delivered above the wide-field preparation alone does not affect the performance of the mice but that it needs to reach the relevant neuronal populations at the right time to become effective.

span.label: short-term memory
span.quote: We propose that short-term memory is present in two different forms: motor-related memory in M2 or sensory-related memory in P

span.label: behavioral strategy
span.quote: We have shown that mice can deploy either an active or passive strategy to solve a texture discrimination task.

span.label: wide-field
span.quote: wide-field fluorescence signals represent bulk signals, summed over neuronal populations

span.label: activeness
span.quote: Here, we find that some mice manage to maintain relatively high performance despite perturbation of one area (M2 or P) whereas other mice show significantly reduced performance. The former mice apparently flexibly switch to the alternative unperturbed strategy whereas the latter mice maintain their strategy. Strategy switches were consistent across days, present also in trials without perturbation and were clearly reflected in corresponding switches between M2- and P-dominated delay maps.

span.label: quiet trials
span.quote: To analyze the delay period, we focused only on quiet trials where the mouse did not move for at least the first second in the delay (starting 0.2 s after beginning of texture retraction; Figure 3A). Trials where the mouse moved during the first second of the delay period where defined as noisy and discarded from the analysis (Figure 1D; bottom trace). For the remaining trials, we detected the first frame where the mouse moved after 1 s into the delay and truncated the F/F traces after this point (Figure S6A, B). Therefore, the data analysis for the delay period excluded any movement-related activity and reflects the population dynamics when the mouse is sitting quietly and maintaining information

span.label: M2
span.quote: We propose that short-term memory is present in two different forms: motor-related memory in M2 or sensory-related memory in P (Figure 8E).

span.label: z-axis drop in focus
span.quote: For a small subset of sessions where the body camera gave low quality images or was missing, we predicted the mouse’s movement based on the z-axis drop in focus (using a 10% drop from baseline in 3 in-focus single cells as criterion; 75% accuracy in labeling trials by validating with move vector from the body camera).

span.label: location of short-term memory - NOT A SINGLE SITE: medio-frontal on active trials and lateral posterior on passive ones, so the answer is conditional on the animal's strategy
span.quote: We propose that short-term memory is present in two different forms: motor-related memory in M2 or sensory-related memory in P

span.label: behavioral strategy - an experimental grouping made from the animal's own conduct: engaging the body toward the approaching texture, or passively awaiting the touch
span.quote: We have shown that mice can deploy either an active or passive strategy to solve a texture discrimination task.

span.label: active versus passive trial - operationalised by thresholding body movement during the sensation period, so the class is fixed by a cut on a continuous measure
span.quote: Classification into active (dark green) and passive (light green) trials is based on movement during the sensation period.

span.label: delay period - AS ANALYSED, NOT AS RUN: restricted to `quiet trials` in which the mouse did not move for at least the first second, with traces truncated at the first movement thereafter. THIS IS A CONTROL, NOT A CONFOUND - the classes are defined by movement during the SENSATION period, and the delay analysis is made movement-free on purpose so that the persistent activity cannot be motor activity
span.quote: To analyze the delay period, we focused only on quiet trials where the mouse did not move for at least the first second in the delay (starting 0.2 s after beginning of texture retraction; Figure 3A). Trials where the mouse moved during the first second of the delay period where defined as noisy and discarded from the analysis (Figure 1D; bottom trace). For the remaining trials, we detected the first frame where the mouse moved after 1 s into the delay and truncated the F/F traces after this point (Figure S6A, B). Therefore, the data analysis for the delay period excluded any movement-related activity and reflects the population dynamics when the mouse is sitting quietly and maintaining information

THIS IS A CONTROL, NOT A CONFOUND - the classes are defined by movement during the SENSATION period, and the delay analysis is made movement-free on purpose so that the persistent activity cannot be motor activity

Trials where the mouse moved during the first second of the delay period where defined as noisy and discarded from the analysis (Figure 1D; bottom trace). For the remaining trials, we detected the first frame where the mouse moved after 1 s into the delay and truncated the F/F traces after this point (Figure S6A, B). Therefore, the data analysis for the delay period excluded any movement-related activity and reflects the population dynamics when the mouse is sitting quietly and maintaining information

span.label: replicates → Chen et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2015 (choice encoding in posterior sensory areas)
span.quote: Thus, consistent with previous reports (Chen et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2015), sensory-related posterior areas S1BC, S2 and RL encode choice shortly after touch for both behavioral strategies.

span.label: replicates → Chen et al., 2013, 2016 (timing of hit/CR discrimination)
span.quote: Discrimination between hit and CR trials occurred within a few hundred milliseconds, in line with previous studies (Chen et al., 2013, 2016).

span.label: extends → Guo et al., 2014; Li et al., 2015 (frontal areas including ALM as the site of short-term memory)
span.quote: In passive trials, M2 as well as other frontal areas (including ALM; Guo et al., 2014; Li et al., 2015) were not activated and could not discriminate trial types (Figure 4), suggesting that they are less important for maintaining information for this type of behavior, at least before any preparatory movements.

span.label: builds-on → Leavitt et al., 2017 (sustained activity encoding working memory is not fully distributed)
span.quote: Maintenance of information in short-term memory is not necessarily tied to one cortical area but is flexibly localized according to behavioral strategy (Leavitt et al., 2017).

span.label: M2 —causes→ behavioral strategy
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.85 — THE PAPER'S GROUPING VARIABLE IS NOT EXOGENOUS, AND THE PAPER IS THE ONE THAT SHOWS IT. The title says strategy DETERMINES where memory is held; silencing the area that holds it makes the animal CHANGE STRATEGY - 'some mice ... apparently flexibly SWITCH TO THE ALTERNATIVE UNPERTURBED STRATEGY', and those switches were 'consistent across days, present also in trials without perturbation and were clearly reflected in corresponding switches between M2- and P-dominated delay maps.' So the arrow runs both ways: strategy selects the site, and removing the site reselects the strategy. Recorded as `causes` in the direction the manipulation establishes, since that is the one an experiment tested.
span.quote: During the delay period we find a clear divergence of activity patterns to either M2 or P depending on behavioral strategy.

span.label: behavioral strategy —operationalised-as→ z-axis drop in focus
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.5 — the record marks this weak — IN A SUBSET OF SESSIONS THE VARIABLE THE WHOLE RESULT IS CONDITIONED ON WAS READ OFF AN IMAGING ARTEFACT: where the body camera failed, movement was predicted from 'the z-axis drop in focus (using a 10% drop from baseline in 3 in-focus single cells as criterion; 75% ACCURACY in labeling trials by validating with move vector from the body camera)'. The accuracy is stated, which is what makes it auditable - but a quarter of those trials carry the wrong class. Low weight for that reason.
span.quote: For a small subset of sessions where the body camera gave low quality images or was missing, we predicted the mouse’s movement based on the z-axis drop in focus (using a 10% drop from baseline in 3 in-focus single cells as criterion; 75% accuracy in labeling trials by validating with move vector from the body camera).

span.label: Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Mann-Whitney U-test
span.term: Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Mann-Whitney U-test
span.quote: In general, non-parametric two-tailed statistical tests were used, Mann-Whitney U-test to compare between two medians from two populations or the Wilcoxon signed rank test to compare a population's median to zero (or between two paired populations).

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: An ANOVA and multiple group correction were used when comparing between more than two groups (Figure 4D-F and Figure S6D).

span.label: F statistic with 95% confidence interval
span.quote: for active strategy P < 0.001; F10,33 = 5.17, 95% confidence interval (CI) [0.04 0.095] for M2

span.label: Kolmogorov-Smirnov test
span.quote: In cases were ANOVA was applied, data was not significantly different from normal distribution (P > 0.05; Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on residuals).

span.label: support vector machine with cross-validation
span.quote: SVM classification was done with 20 cross-validations and trial label shuffling (see relevant section above).

span.label: label-shuffling permutation test
span.quote: To test for significance, we shuffled between hit and CR labels (while maintaining active and passive labels) and performed the same SVM, resulting in an accuracy of 48.5 ± 4.2 and 50.4 ± 3.8 (mean ± s.e.m), i.e. chance level, for active and passive trials, respectively.

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: To reduce noise, we initially performed a principal component analysis (PCA) analysis on the delay maps and each pixel (feature) was represented by the top 25 PCs

span.label: ROC analysis / area under the curve
span.term: ROC analysis / area under the curve
span.quote: We calculated a receiver operating characteristics (ROC) curve for each pixel in a given area and calculated its area under the curve (AUC).

span.label: correlation coefficient
span.quote: In addition, d’ performance positively correlated with activeness (Figure 1H; r = 0.6; P < 0.001)

span.label: Bonferroni correction
span.quote: Interestingly, for passive trials, SVM accuracy was at chance level when we applied the SVM only to pixels in the frontal cortex (Figure 4F; P > 0.05; signed-rank test compared to 50%; Bonferroni corrected; n = 39 imaging sessions from 5 passive mice).

span.label: Which cortical area held the delay-period memory depended on the mouse's behavioural strategy: persistent activity sat medio-frontally (M2) on active trials but in a lateral posterior area on passive trials.
span.quote: During the delay, in contrast, persistent cortical activity was located medio-frontally in active trials but in a lateral posterior area in passive trials.

span.label: The posterior whisker areas encoded the animal's choice soon after touch under both strategies, so the strategy difference appeared only later, during the delay.
span.quote: texture-or passively awaited the touch. Independent of strategy, whisker-related posterior areas encoded choice early after touch. During the delay, in contrast,

span.label: Optogenetically silencing M2 or area P lowered task performance only in trials run with the strategy that area supports, and left the other strategy unaffected.
span.quote: In summary, perturbation of one area (M2 or P) decreased performance exclusively when the mouse used the associated strategy (Figure 7D; P < 0.05; signed-rank test).

span.label: Silencing M2 and area P together dropped all four VGAT-ChR2 mice to performance indistinguishable from the non-expert threshold, which single-area silencing had not done.
span.quote: All four mice significantly reduced their performance upon ChR2 activation (P < 0.001; signed-rank test), down to levels not significantly different from the expert threshold (Figure 7F; P > 0.05; signed-rank test).

span.label: Some mice escaped a perturbation by switching behavioural strategy rather than losing performance, one passive mouse turning active during the perturbation sessions.
span.quote: Notably, however, this mouse very efficiently switched its strategy from passive to active in the perturbation sessions (Figure 6Fii, iii; P < 0.001; Mann-Whitney U-test).

span.label: The two memory sites hold different content: the motor-sensory index was positive in M2 (activity grouped by the upcoming action) and negative in area P (activity grouped by the past texture).
span.quote: MSI was significantly positive in M2 and significantly negative in P (Figure 8D; P < 0.05; Wilcoxon signed-rank test), implying that each area encodes a different type of short-term memory

span.label: On passive trials a classifier restricted to frontal-cortex pixels could not tell hit from correct-rejection trials at all, showing short-term memory need not reside in frontal cortex.
span.quote: Interestingly, for passive trials, SVM accuracy was at chance level when we applied the SVM only to pixels in the frontal cortex (Figure 4F; P > 0.05; signed-rank test compared to 50%; Bonferroni corrected; n = 39 imaging sessions from 5 passive mice).

span.label: The more a mouse used the active strategy the better it discriminated textures, and passive mice needed roughly twice as many sessions to reach expert level.
span.quote: In addition, d’ performance positively correlated with activeness (Figure 1H; r = 0.6; P < 0.001)

span.label: activeness
span.quote: ‘Activeness’ was defined as the percentage of active hit trials and derived for each imaging session

span.label: active versus passive trial
span.quote: A trial was labeled (unrelated to hit or CR) as ‘active’ if the mouse was moving for at least 0.5 seconds during the sensation period (-1 s to 2 s relative to texture stop) and ‘passive’ otherwise.

span.label: motor-sensory index (MSI)
span.quote: MSI ranges from -1 to 1 where positive values indicate greater encoding of motor-related information (similar activity for similar future action) whereas negative values indicate greater encoding of sensory-related information (similar activity for similar past stimuli).

span.label: posterior area P
span.quote: we refer to this region as ‘posterior area P’ (or brief ‘P’; see Discussion; see also additional retinotopic alignment in Figure S7B)

span.label: optogenetic silencing light delivered during the delay period
span.term: optogenetic silencing light delivered during the delay period
span.quote: Light was randomly delivered in 50% of the trials during the delay period

span.label: texture identity (P100 rough 'go' versus P1200 smooth 'no-go' sandpaper)
span.term: texture identity (P100 rough 'go' versus P1200 smooth 'no-go' sandpaper)
span.quote: Each trial started with an auditory cue (2 beeps at 2 kHz, 100-ms duration with 50-ms interval), signaling the approach of either two types of sandpapers (grit size P100: rough texture; P1200: smooth texture) to the mouse’s whiskers as ‘go’ or ‘no-go’ textures (pseudo-randomly presented with no more than 3 repetitions).

span.label: layer 2/3 neuronal calcium activity
span.quote: Using wide-field and single-cell calcium imaging we measured layer 2/3 neuronal activity in mice performing a whisker-based texture discrimination task with delayed response.

span.label: discrimination performance (d-prime)
span.quote: Performance was quantified as d-prime (Chen et al., 2013)

span.label: body movement during the delay period (held at zero by excluding moving epochs)
span.term: body movement during the delay period (held at zero by excluding moving epochs)
span.quote: Therefore, the data analysis for the delay period excluded any movement-related activity and reflects the population dynamics when the mouse is sitting quietly and maintaining information to guide its future action.

span.label: 16 and 82% — range of activeness (percentage of hit trials with body movement at texture touch) across the eight imaged mice
span.quote: ‘Activeness’, quantified as the percentage of hit trials with body movements prior and during the texture touch, varied across mice between 16 and 82%

span.label: 60-88% — accuracy of the classifier separating hit from correct-rejection delay maps, across mice and both strategies
span.quote: accuracy ranged from 60-88% in all mice for active and passive trials (Figure 4B).

span.label: 48.5 ± 4.2 and 50.4 ± 3.8 — classifier accuracy after shuffling trial labels, i.e. the chance baseline for active and passive trials
span.quote: To test for significance, we shuffled between hit and CR labels (while maintaining active and passive labels) and performed the same SVM, resulting in an accuracy of 48.5 ± 4.2 and 50.4 ± 3.8 (mean ± s.e.m), i.e. chance level, for active and passive trials, respectively.

span.label: r = 0.6 — correlation between a session's activeness and the mouse's d-prime discrimination performance
span.quote: In addition, d’ performance positively correlated with activeness (Figure 1H; r = 0.6; P < 0.001)

span.label: 6.9 ± 0.3 weeks — training time needed before imaging, across the eight mice
span.quote: During training, an increasing delay was gradually introduced over weeks (Figure 1B; training time 6.9 ± 0.3 weeks; mean ± s.e.m.; n = 8 mice).

span.label: 1.2-4.5 s — range of enforced delay durations mice could withhold licking for
span.quote: Mice learned to withhold licking for up to several seconds (range of 1.2-4.5 s).

span.label: 2.89° ± 0.36° vs. 0.95° ± 0.14° — whisking envelope around texture arrival on active versus passive trials
span.quote: mean whisking envelope from -1 to +1 seconds relative to texture stop: 2.89° ± 0.36° vs. 0.95° ± 0.14°; P < 0.05

span.label: 30 — total adult male mice used across imaging, control and optogenetic experiments
span.quote: A total of 30 adult male mice (1-9 months old) were used in this study.
